Content, BIOS/firmware handling, controls, audio/video pacing, saves and state round trips, reset and unload behavior, frontend integration, compatibility, licensing review, and sustained performance remain target-runtime and human gates. Publication remains disabled regardless of local byte reproducibility.

The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and independent native-local build-core run reproduced the package, metadata, build logs, and both ABI artifacts byte for byte. Both profiles satisfy the exact fail-closed VecX compile, ordered-link, source, native-version, metadata-replacement, dependency, and diagnostic proof.

The pristine source is commit 8f671cc9d737f2890c3ce19e177e2984dcae121f, tree 49ae584713edede2a70792ecf6cb744b11fff2e6, with no submodules. The exact HAS_GPU=0 software recipe binds upstream's native leading-space short hash across all four C compile commands, requires the complete ordered link invocation, exposes version 1.2 8f671cc, and installs metadata replacement SHA-256 2f22e8069a304878b52aeb5d7f789812bf271c61e5c41e0cb0fbd6acb5d28c1a.

ARM64 requires GLIBC_2.17 and records the AArch64 loader and libc. ARMHF is EABI5 hard-float, reaches GLIBC_2.4, and records libc and libm. Neither shared object depends on a GL-family library or has a PT_INTERP; loader, provider, rootfs, frontend, and target execution remain runtime gates.
Resolver metadata declares GPLv3. Any public distribution or release remains a human legal and policy gate even though the local builds reproduce.

No external firmware is declared or packaged; the core uses its source-embedded standard Vectrex system image. Vectrex content loading, software video, audio, controls, save states, pacing, compatibility, and sustained performance remain target-runtime gates.

The software-only Unix recipe produces one shared artifact per ABI and provides no basis for device-specific duplicate builds. ARM64 is build-identity-bound only to ra64-universal-v1 and ARMHF only to ra32-a30-v1; all device views remain ineligible pending provider and target-runtime evidence.
